title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 33 (Issue of Application Forms for Securities)

content.overview: Section 33 requires that no form of application for the purchase of any of the securities of a company may be issued unless it is accompanied by an abridged prospectus, subject to limited exceptions. A person is entitled to a copy of the prospectus on request before the closing of the subscription list and offer; default attracts a penalty.
content.glance: Application forms must be accompanied by an abridged prospectus (with statutory exceptions); prospectus copy on request; penalty for default.
content.study: No form of application for the purchase of any securities of a company may be issued unless such form is accompanied by an abridged prospectus. Exceptions apply where the form is issued in connection with a bona fide invitation to a person to enter into an underwriting agreement, or where the securities are not offered to the public. Any person who requests a copy of the prospectus before the closing of the subscription list and offer is entitled to be furnished with one. Contravention attracts a penalty of fifty thousand rupees for each default. Current-law framing: identify issue of an application form; test whether an abridged prospectus accompanied it or an exception applies; check prospectus-copy requests.

sections.heading: Abridged Prospectus Requirement
sections.body: An application form for purchase of company securities must be accompanied by an abridged prospectus.

sections.heading: Exceptions
sections.body: The requirement does not apply to forms issued in connection with a bona fide underwriting invitation or where the securities are not offered to the public.

sections.heading: Prospectus Copy on Request
sections.body: A person is entitled to a copy of the prospectus on request before the closing of the subscription list and offer.

sections.heading: Penalty
sections.body: Default attracts a penalty of fifty thousand rupees for each default.

provisions.title: Issue of application forms for securities

examples.title: Form with abridged prospectus
examples.body: A company issues application forms for a public issue together with an abridged prospectus. Section 33 is complied with.

examples.title: Form without abridged prospectus
examples.body: Application forms for a public offer are circulated without an abridged prospectus and no exception applies. Section 33 is breached.

hypotheticals.question: Must every application form carry a full prospectus?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 33 requires an abridged prospectus, not the full prospectus; a full copy must be supplied on request before closure of the offer.

distinctions.title: Abridged prospectus with application form (s. 33) vs full prospectus content (s. 26)
distinctions.right: Full statutory content, dating, signing and ROC filing

misconceptions.trap: Application forms can be issued freely without any prospectus material.
misconceptions.correction: Section 33 requires an abridged prospectus to accompany the form unless a statutory exception applies.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 33 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify issue of application form. II. Check abridged prospectus or exception. III. Address prospectus-copy request. IV. Apply penalty if default. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Form issue facts; abridged prospectus status; exceptions; request compliance; penalty; precise relief.

examTips: Mention the right to a full prospectus copy on request.
